title: How to Do a Side Plank for Beginners (Side Ab Workout at Home)
intro: The side plank is a plank done on your side that trains your side abs, side glutes and shoulders. It's great for body stability and you can do it in your living room without any equipment.
muscles: Side abs (obliques), deep core muscles, side glutes (gluteus medius) and shoulders. The side plank strengthens your waist area, but it doesn't specifically remove waist fat. Fat is reduced from your whole body through eating and movement.
steps: Lie on your side, with your elbow directly under your shoulder.
Stack your feet on top of each other, or place your top foot in front of the bottom foot for more stability.
Push your hips up until your body is straight from head to feet.
Place your top hand on your hip or reach it straight up.
Hold and breathe slowly, then switch sides.
mistakes: Hips dropping to the floor. Think of pushing your hips towards the ceiling.
Body twisting forward or backward. Make sure your chest faces forward.
Shoulder shrugging up to your ear. Push the floor away with your forearm to keep your shoulder stable.
easier: Do a knee side plank: knees bent at 90 degrees, supporting yourself on your knee and elbow. You still need to lift your hips.
harder: Straighten your legs and slowly lift your top leg. Or lower and raise your hips 8-10 times in the side plank position.
dose: Beginner: 2-3 sets x 10-20 seconds on each side, rest 30-60 seconds. Do it 2-3 times a week.
safety: Stop if you feel sharp shoulder pain or numbness in your arm. If you have shoulder problems, chronic lower back pain or have just given birth, get advice from a doctor or physiotherapist first.

faq.q: Can the side plank remove fat on the sides of my waist (love handles)?
faq.a: The side plank strengthens your side muscles, but you can't choose which fat goes first. Waist fat comes down when your whole body loses fat. Focus on food portions, daily steps and strength training consistently.

faq.q: Why does my shoulder feel uncomfortable?
faq.a: Usually your elbow isn't directly under your shoulder, or your shoulder is sinking too much. Fix your elbow position and push the floor away. If it still hurts, switch to the knee version or stop.

faq.q: Do I have to do both sides?
faq.a: Yes. Hold for the same time on each side. Usually one side is weaker, so start with the weaker side first.
